summary: Zhiyi Yang is a sinologist who studied at Peking University, Princeton University (PhD under Martin Kern and others), and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg. She held posts at Erlangen-Nuremberg and Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 2015).

Zhonghui Cui works in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and sinology. She earned an MA from SOAS University of London and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, where she served as a teaching consultant (attested 2013).

Zhongxin Jiang (1942–2002) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University (~1962–1968) under Xianlin Ji. He held positions at Peking University, the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978–2002), and Soka University (~1998–1999).
Zijie Li specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Komazawa University and served as a DC special research fellow for the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (both attested 2015).
Zong Rinpoche (1905–1984) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Trijang Rinpoche and held a post at Ganden Shartse Monastery (~1937–1946).

Zongsan Mou (1909–1995) was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking University (~1929–1933) under Shili Xiong. He taught at Zhejiang University, National Taiwan University, National Taiwan Normal University, Tunghai University, and the New Asia Institute (~1974–1995).

Zsóka Gelle is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Vienna. She held posts at the Tibet House Foundation, the East-West Research Institute, Eötvös Loránd University (2014–2016), and the Budapest Centre for Buddhist Studies (2014–2016).

Zuiei Ito (1942–2020) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1965–1970). He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Waseda University, and Rissho University (~1975–2013).

Zuiho Yamaguchi (1926–2023) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1953) and under Rolf Alfred Stein and Jacques Bacot. He taught at Nagoya University and the University of Tokyo (1970–1986).

Zuiryu Nakamura (1915–1997) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Rissho University (~1937–1940) and under Susumu Yamaguchi (1944). In 1945, he became a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University.

Édouard Chavannes (1865–1918) was a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1885–1888). He served as a professor at the Collège de France from 1893 to 1918.

Édouard Huber (1879–1914) worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, studying at the University of Paris, ENLOV, and the Collège de France (~1899–1902). He was an interim professor of Chinese at EFEO (~1905–1912).

Émile Benveniste (1902–1976) was a linguist, Iranist, and Indologist who studied at the University of Paris under Antoine Meillet. He held positions at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1927–1969) and the Collège de France (1937–1972).

Émile Burnouf (1821–1907) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at ENS, the French School at Athens, and under Jean-Louis and Eugène Burnouf. He held a professorship at the University of Nancy and its Faculté des lettres (~1854–1867).
Émile Senart (1847–1928) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology who studied under Theodor Benfey (~1867–1868). He served as president of the Société Asiatique from 1908 to 1928.

Étienne Balázs (1905–1963) specialized in sinology, history, and archaeology, studying under Otto Franke in 1923. He held posts at the CNRS (1949) and as a professor of Chinese economic history at the University of Paris (~1955–1963).

Étienne Lamotte (1903–1983) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at KU Leuven, Sapienza, and Paris institutions under Louis de La Vallée Poussin and others. He had a long career at KU Leuven (~1932–1962).

Ñāṇavīra Thera (1920–1965) studied Buddhist studies and philosophy under Pelene Siri Vajirañāṇa (~1949–1955). Educated at Wellington College and Magdalene College (~1938–1940), he served in the Royal Artillery (1939–1941) and Intelligence Corps (1941–1945).
Ülo Valk is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tartu (~1981–1986). He took up a post at Tartu (~1991) and served as editor of Numen (~2007–2014).
